Phoenix-chaser/CodeAgent-R.body:
# CodeAgent-R

**Post-training and execution-based evaluation for code-repair models** · [English](https://github.com/Phoenix-chaser/CodeAgent-R/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md)

CodeAgent-R is a reproducible post-training and evaluation pipeline for code repair: a frozen task pool, execution-based scoring, QLoRA SFT / DPO / RFT, model selection on dev, and paired comparison against the base model (Base) on the frozen test set. All published experiments were evaluated on 104 self-written single-file Python repair tasks using **Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct**. Qwen3.5-9B is also supported. It has no experimental results yet, so run a smoke test before the first run.

**Conclusion: the pipeline runs end to end, but it did not measure a reliable improvement.** On the 20 frozen test tasks, Base fixed 12 and teacher-distillation SFT fixed 13. Averaged over three training seeds, the gain is 1.7 percentage points, with a 95% interval of [0, +5]. Two of the seeds selected Base on dev. All three DPO rounds failed to exceed SFT. The test set has only 20 tasks, all self-written, and this scale does not support generalization claims.

[Method comparison](#方法对比) · [Three-seed reproduction](#三种子复现) · [Experiment evolution](#实验演进) · [Training and evaluation pipeline](#训练与评测流程) · [How results are kept credible](#结果如何保证可信) · [Quick start](#本地快速开始)

## How results are kept credible

- **Scoring**: a pass means that every test in the batch generated from the reference solution runs against the candidate and passes. The exit code, the pytest summary line, and the junit XML must agree on all three counts. Early exits, skipped cases, or fewer collected cases are all judged as failures.
- **Isolation**: candidate code runs in a kernel Landlock sandbox. The workspace is read-only, the real HOME and /proc are unreadable, and TCP connections are refused. Runs are constrained by CPU time, memory, process count, and process-group timeout cleanup, and environment variables are built from an allowlist. If the kernel does not support the sandbox, the run degrades, and the isolation actually in effect is recorded in the scoring details.
- **Statistics**: the bootstrap samples by source group, the same independent unit used for task splitting and leakage checks.
- **Evidence**: `scripts/export_evidence.py` exports local artifacts to `docs/evidence/` after redacting them. Once the evidence bundle is committed, CI recomputes the conclusions from the per-task results using `scripts/verify_evidence.py`.
- **CI**: lint, CPU tests, evidence review, and privacy checks. See [checks.yml](https://github.com/Phoenix-chaser/CodeAgent-R/blob/HEAD/.github/workflows/checks.yml).

SimomYung/unpack_huawei_package.body:
# Huawei Phone Firmware Package Unpacking Tool
## 1. Introduction:
- Huawei Android system packages (before HarmonyOS 5) use the update.app format. This format can be unpacked with HuaweiUpdateExtractor to obtain all partition images.
- Starting with HarmonyOS 5, Huawei firmware packages use the new update.bin format. This format cannot be unpacked with HuaweiUpdateExtractor. Opening it in a hex editor shows that it is the standard OpenHarmony upgrade package format.
- Although OpenHarmony provides an unpacking tool, [update_packaging_tools library](https://gitee.com/openharmony/update_packaging_tools), running it produces no output. Adding a main program after the code makes it run normally, but when a partition is very large (system.img, >1G), a data offset parsing error occurs, so the unpacked image is much smaller than the actual size.
- After reading the official code, I wrote unpack_huawei_package.py in Python. This project requires no dependencies to be installed. If you don't want to install Python, the project also provides a ready-to-run exe program.
- Place update.bin in the same directory as the program. You can also specify the update.bin file path by modifying line 5 of unpack_huawei_package.py.
## 2. update.bin File Structure Analysis:
- update.bin comes in two forms, L2 and non-L2. HarmonyOS 5 uses the L2 form, so only the L2 structure is parsed.
- The first 178 B is the file header, which contains version and build time information.
- The next 2 B is a little-endian length-4 value indicating the total length of the partition information.
- Partition information has two possible lengths.
- (1) Each partition information entry in the L2 form is 87 B. Bytes 48-55, 8 B in total, are a 16-bit hexadecimal little-endian value representing the length of each partition. The final 32 B are the GUID and UUID.
- (2) Each partition information entry in the non-L2 form is 71 B.
- Based on the length of each partition information entry, you can quickly tell whether your update.bin is in L2 format. You can open the file with [Hexadecimal Editor](http://wxmedit.github.io/zh_CN/downloads.html). If each partition information entry is 87 B, meaning the interval between two "/" characters is 87 B, it is the L2 form; otherwise it is the non-L2 form.
- The next 16 B is the fixed content "update/info.bin ".
- The next 2 B is a little-endian hexadecimal length-4 value that determines how the following signature is handled.

## What this tool does

**Agy Powertools** is an enhancement plugin for Antigravity 2.0. It attaches directly inside the client through a local debugging interface, reads local SQLite and JSONL session records, and adds several useful features to Antigravity 2.0 without modifying the client's installed files or opening external web pages.

It mainly addresses four pain points in everyday use of Antigravity:

1. **Fully English interface with low information density**: The native menus and settings are all in English. The chat area's default line height and paragraph spacing are loose, so only a little code and tool output fits on one screen.
2. **Multi-step tasks lack clear stage feedback**: When the agent calls tools in succession, it either stays silent for a long time with no visible progress, or keeps piling transitional commentary into the body text, which gets in the way of reading the final answer.
3. **No real-time context window display**: In long conversations, it is hard to see context usage, cache hit rate, generation speed, and details of individual errors. There is also no central place to view the 5-hour limit, the weekly limit, and cumulative token usage.
4. **Conversation forking and correcting steps are cumbersome**: When you want to edit an already-sent prompt and retry, or branch off from a satisfying answer in the middle to explore a different approach, there is no convenient native entry point.

# YuriQuant

**A-share full-market quantitative research and production system.**

From raw market data to a daily actionable ranking list, it covers the complete pipeline: data collection, factor research, model training, portfolio construction, backtesting, risk attribution, production scheduling, and report delivery. The full pipeline can run on a single machine.

The system is designed around three principles: **backtests use no future information, research conclusions can be reproduced out of sample, and strategies can go directly into production.** Research code and production code share the same data layer, factor layer, and backtesting engine. Any strategy that appears in a report can be run in daily production with the same code.

---

## 1. Core Strategies

### 1.1 yqcore Finalized Strategy

Three configurations of the same signal family. They differ in position concentration and the execution layer. Backtest window: 2019-01 to 2026-09. Initial capital: 1,000,000 yuan.

| Tier | Form | Holdings | Annualized | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Annual turnover |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Broad tier** `breadth` | Full-factor orthogonal panel + monthly Top10% equal weight, with buffer band | avg. 614 stocks | **21.81%** | 1.013 | 26.6% | 17.1% |
| **Concentrated tier** `focus-k15` | Four-horizon fused signal + TopK15, with buffer band | 15 stocks | **29.60%** | 1.113 | 38.2% | 87.6% |
| **Small-capital tier** `focus-k8` | Same as above + at most 1 stock per industry | avg. 5.9 stocks | **36.58%** | 1.271 | 36.3% | 92.4% |

The three tiers should not be ranked by return alone. # Ktown4u Cloud Auto-Scraping (GitHub Actions)

Let GitHub automatically scrape Ktown4u signing-event sales 24/7 in the cloud, with the data stored in the repository.
Even if your computer loses its internet connection, you can view or download the full history by opening the repository whenever you're online.

## File structure (place as-is in the repository)
```
your-repo/
├─ .github/workflows/track.yml   # Scheduled task (every 5 minutes)
├─ ktown4u_ci.py                 # Scraping script
├─ track_config.json             # Config: which events to track
└─ data/                         # Auto-generated: track_<event number>.csv
```

## One-time setup (about 5 minutes)

1. **Create a GitHub repository** and select **Public**.
   > Why public: Actions in public repositories are **free with unlimited usage**; private repositories only get 2000 minutes per month, which won't last long.
   > Signing sales data is not sensitive, so making it public is fine.

2. **Upload these three files** (keep the directory structure above): `.github/workflows/track.yml`, `ktown4u_ci.py`, `track_config.json`.
   - Via the web: repo page → Add file → Upload files, then drag in the contents of the `cloud/` folder
     (be careful not to drop the `.github/workflows/track.yml` directory level).

3. Open the **Actions** tab → if prompted, click **"I understand my workflows, enable them"** to enable them.

4. **Enter the event numbers you want to track**: edit `events` in `track_config.json`, for example:
   ```json
   { "shopNo": 164, "interval": 10, "burstSeconds": 200, "events": [44469917, 44468447] }
   ```
   - Where to get event numbers: use "Load current event / Search" in the local web version, `ktown4u_app.py`.
   - After you commit and save, the next run will start tracking these events.

Done! After that, it **runs automatically once every 5 minutes**, and within each run it scrapes every 10 seconds. Data keeps being appended to `data/track_<event number>.csv` (columns: `time, member, sales, delta`).

Welcome to **阿卡迪亚:永恒之门** (Arcadia Eternity)

This project is a battle simulation system for 约瑟传说 (赛尔号2). It provides an online web page, a team editor, and a desktop content-pack workbench.

The web version uses HTML5, and the desktop client uses Electron. The battle core is shared by the Node server, the CLI, and local battles. The current development and integration branch is `main`.

Supports local AI battles, friend rooms, and regular matchmaking.

[创作者文档](https://battle-docs.yuuinih.com/) · [霜击教程](https://battle-docs.yuuinih.com/frost-strike) · [战斗 SDK 参考](https://battle-docs.yuuinih.com/sdk/)

You can learn about the project's architecture and some of its design philosophy in the DeepWiki linked above.

QQ group: 805146068

## Related libraries

- [seer2-pet-animator](https://github.com/arcadia-star/seer2-pet-animator) Animation container for reusing the original game's resources
- [seer2-resource](https://github.com/arcadia-eternity/seer2-resource) Game resources from the original game, organized and used in this project

## Quick start

### Start a test battle

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build:package
pnpm build:cli
pnpm cli battle simulate -1 testteam.yaml -2 testteam.yaml --json
```

### Start the server

```sh
# Build dependencies, then start the backend server (no Redis or external database needed; uses SQLite by default)
pnpm install
pnpm build:prod
pnpm run cli server --port 8102 --server-id arcadia-local

```

Open `http://localhost:8102` to use the companion web page. For development mode, the following commands can replace the startup command above; run the backend and frontend in separate terminals:

```sh
pnpm cli server --headless --cors-origin http://localhost:5173
pnpm web:dev
```

bunkmr/mac-mouse-without-borders.body:
# MWB Mac Client

A macOS client written in **Swift** that connects to the Windows-side **Mouse Without Borders** (built into PowerToys).
It lets your Mac act as a bidirectional node in the MWB mesh: **keyboard and mouse control between Windows and Mac, clipboard text sync, and drag-and-drop file transfer in both directions**.

> Why Swift instead of C#: the MWB protocol is essentially "a stream of bytes over a socket" and is language-independent.
> Injecting and capturing input on the Mac side requires calling CoreGraphics, which is cleanest to do directly from Swift with no C# P/Invoke bridge, and it can also directly produce a native `.app`.

> **File transfer does not use any custom protocol.** It goes through MWB's own native clipboard/file channel
> (the main channel port minus 1), so the Windows side does not need any extra program or script installed.

---

## Implemented / To do

| Module | Status | Notes |
|------|------|------|
| TCP connection + encrypted handshake | ✅ | Verified legacy scheme: AES-256-CBC, PBKDF2-HMAC-**SHA1** (50000 iterations), **fixed** salt/IV, no plaintext salt+IV header |
| Packet encoding/decoding (32/64 bytes) | ✅ | Byte-for-byte aligned with PowerToys `App/Core`; 4-byte `Type`, 16-byte union area, 32-byte machine name |
| Mouse injection (move/click/wheel) | ✅ | `CGEventPost` (requires Accessibility/Input Monitoring authorization) |
| Keyboard injection | ✅ | Windows VK to Mac keycode mapping |
| Local input capture (reverse control of Win) | ✅ | `CGEventTap` (requires authorization). **The built-in trackpad can also cross screens** (2026-11-23, see below) |
| Trackpad driving the remote machine | ✅ | Trackpad and mouse take raw deltas and are calibrated **separately** (`RawPointerSource`), without interfering with each other |
| Cursor lock / edge switching | ✅ | While controlling the remote machine, the local cursor is **hidden** (`CGDisplayHideCursor` + **private property `SetsCursorInBackground` to unlock**, reasserted at event level at 100Hz), and event coordinates are rewritten to pin the cursor to an anchor point. Criterion: `CGCursorIsVisible()`; self-test measured **100% hidden samples, max offset 0px**. See below for details |
| Clipboard text sync | ✅ | Two channels: `ClipboardText(124)` fragmented + change notification `Clipboard(69)` |

Supports 100 devices, Kafka, HDFS, MySQL, Redis.
esion0621/predictive-maintenance-platfor.body:
# Industrial Equipment Predictive Maintenance Platform

---

An industrial IoT predictive maintenance system based on the Lambda architecture. The platform simulates sensor data streams from 100 devices and uses Flink CEP rule matching and a random forest model to detect anomalies in real time. Spark trains models offline and hot-updates them, and the project provides a complete backend API and frontend visualization interface.

## 🎯 Core Features

> The following features have been verified only in the project's built-in simulated data environment, to demonstrate the end-to-end pipeline and architectural design. They do not represent production-grade SLAs.

- **Dual-channel alerting with CEP and models**: After Flink consumes Kafka data, CEP rules (continuous temperature rise R1, simultaneous vibration + current excess R2, sudden pressure drop R3) and random forest model inference run **in parallel**. The two alert streams are merged via `union`, and the frontend distinguishes them by the `source` field as `CEP` / `MODEL`. CEP handles millisecond-level detection of known fault patterns, while the model provides probability scoring for unknown anomalies, and neither blocks the other.
- **Real-time model inference**: Features are extracted with a hand-written `KeyedProcessFunction` over a 30s window / 10s slide (each device keeps only one `ListState` buffer and one merged timer, avoiding the state amplification of the built-in sliding window, which would maintain about 3 overlapping windows at 30s/10s). The random forest model is hot-loaded via HDFS/broadcast mechanisms and outputs anomaly probabilities in real time.
- **State-machine simulated data generation**: The producer is based on a `DeviceState` state machine, combining random walk, mean reversion, and probabilistic fault injection to generate time-correlated sensor data for end-to-end pipeline validation. **It does not represent the noise, missing values, or concept drift of real sensor data.**
- **Offline model training**: Spark reads historical HDFS data daily and trains anomaly detection and remaining useful life models using combined multi-condition labels. **A new model replaces the current version only if its core validation-set metric (such as F1 for the anomaly class) improves by more than 2%**, to avoid metric oscillation.
- **Complete data service**: Spring Boot REST API that aggregates real-time data from Redis and statistical results from MySQL.
- **Visual monitoring**: React + ECharts display device status, CEP/model alerts, health trends, and reports.

---

fragrans-maotou/zentao-mcp.body:
# ZenTao (禅道) MCP Server

A project management toolset service for ZenTao built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It uses a domain-layered modular architecture and lets AI assistants (such as Antigravity, Claude, etc.) call the ZenTao API directly through the standard protocol.

---

## Quick Start

This service is launched with `npx`, pulling from GitHub. Before use, you need **Node.js (≥ 18)** and **Git** installed locally. Installing these two pieces of software, as well as cloning this public repository, **does not require a GitHub account or login**.

### 1. Install Node.js

1. Open [https://nodejs.org/](https://nodejs.org/) and download the LTS installer (choose `.msi` on Windows).
2. Click through the installation, keeping **Add to PATH** checked.
3. After installation, **reopen** your terminal or MCP client and run:

```bash
node -v
npx -v
```

If version numbers appear, you're set (Node must be ≥ 18).

### 2. Install Git

1. Open [https://git-scm.com/download/win](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and download and install Git for Windows.
2. Keep the default installation options (it is added to PATH automatically).
3. **No need** to register or log in to GitHub. This repository is public, so `npx git+https://...` only pulls anonymously and will not ask for a username or password. If a GitHub login window pops up after installation, simply close it.
4. After reopening the terminal, run:

```bash
git --version
```

If a version number appears, you're set.

### 3. Configure the MCP Client

Copy the block below into your MCP client configuration and change only the three environment variables. No manual cloning or compiling is needed.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zentao": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "git+https://github.com/fragrans-maotou/zentao-mcp.git"],
      "env": {
        "ZENTAO_BASE": "http://your-zentao-host/zentao",
        "ZENTAO_ACCOUNT": "your_account",
        "ZENTAO_PASSWORD": "your_password"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# yt-dlp Music Import

Songloft JS plugin — import playlists from YouTube, Bilibili, SoundCloud and other platforms into Songloft via [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp).

## Features

- **Playlist import**: paste a link to extract playlist metadata and import it into the music library
- **On-demand playback**: imported as online songs; the audio URL is resolved and cached on first playback
- **Download locally**: optionally download songs as local files for offline use
- **Multi-platform support**: supports all platforms supported by yt-dlp (1000+)
- **Automatic deduplication**: the same video will not be imported twice

## Installation

Install from the Songloft plugin management page, or manually download the `.jsplugin.zip` file from [Releases](https://github.com/hanxi/songloft-plugin-ytdlp/blob/HEAD/../../releases).

### Plugin source URL

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanxi/songloft-plugin-ytdlp/main/registry.json
```

In Songloft Settings → JS Plugins → Plugin Sources, add the above URL to receive updates automatically.

## Usage

1. Install the yt-dlp binary on the plugin settings page (automatically downloads the version for your platform)
2. On the import page, paste a playlist or video link
3. Click "Extract" to get the song list
4. Choose "Import only" or "Import and download", then run the import

For Linux x86-64 and ARM64, the automatic installation and manual download links select the upstream binary according to the server's libc. If the settings page shows "Cannot run", click "Reinstall yt-dlp" and check the error details below the status.

Automatic installation verifies the download size and runs the new file to check its version before replacing the original file. If a file size mismatch is reported, you can switch the GitHub proxy and try again.

In "Download Manager" you can pause, resume, or cancel batches. Cancelling stops subsequent songs and retries; a single download that has already started will continue to completion, showing "Cancelling" in the meantime. Downloaded files are kept; after a batch finishes, you can clear its records and start a new batch.

### Smart speaker search source

The "Search Test" on the settings page searches for songs and verifies whether direct audio links can be obtained. If the service requires login, the test will prompt you to configure Cookies. When a smart speaker has search-result import enabled, song information can be obtained first and Songloft resolves the audio at playback time; "Play directly without importing" still requires the search source to obtain a direct link on the spot.

# 忘却的旋律启动器

**经典国产 Minecraft Java 版启动器“忘却的旋律”的现代独立重制版。**

The code and documentation were written by AI and may contain errors, omissions, or compatibility issues. Please back up your saves, mods, and configuration before use. When reporting issues, provide the version number, reproduction steps, and redacted logs. Do not submit account files, passwords, or tokens.

## Project Overview

忘却的旋律启动器 is an Electron-based Minecraft Java Edition launcher built from scratch. It keeps the quiet, compact character of the old launcher and rewrites the internals using modern workflows for downloads, accounts, Java runtimes, mod loaders, and game launching.

This project is an independent tribute. It is not an official update or continuation of the original project, and it does not use the original source code. It has no affiliation with or endorsement from the original author, Mojang Studios, or Microsoft.

## Name and History

忘却的旋律 was one of the many third-party launchers widely used in the early Chinese Minecraft community. Public sources generally describe it as an 易语言 program that was popular around 2012, known for its small size, simple interface, replaceable backgrounds, and convenient game configuration. Public sources commonly cite `5.31` as the final version and state that the project stopped being maintained in 2014.

Existing records are incomplete, and some claims contradict each other. For example, the same encyclopedia page mentions both 2009 and 2012. Therefore, this document treats “around 2012,” the final version `5.31`, and the 2014 end of maintenance as information circulating in the community, not as facts verified from primary sources.

The current repository is a completely new implementation. Its version numbers and code history are unrelated to the historical launcher.

mengqi1436/dsh-db-tool.body:
# dsh-db-tool

[English](https://github.com/mengqi1436/dsh-db-tool/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md) | Simplified Chinese

DSH host plugin. Safely operate databases from within chat: nine database types, fine-grained project-level authorization, dangerous-operation confirmation, and full audit logging. Includes a companion sidebar admin console and SQL console.

## Feature flow

The complete path of a database operation, from entry point to audit persistence. The chat tool and the sidebar share one set of semantics, and every operation must pass two gates: project-level authorization and statement-level risk classification:

[Open interactive version](https://github.com/mengqi1436/dsh-db-tool/blob/HEAD/assets/feature-flow.html) — supports zoom, drag, path highlighting, and clicking nodes to view source-code evidence.

> Questions or suggestions? [Open an Issue](https://github.com/mengqi1436/dsh-db-tool/issues/new/choose).

---

## Supported databases

| Category | Databases |
| --- | --- |
| Relational | MySQL, PostgreSQL, GaussDB, SQLite, Oracle, 达梦 DM, SQL Server |
| NoSQL | Redis, MongoDB |

Connection, metadata browsing, querying, and preview cover nine database types. Data transfer is tiered by capability: eight databases (MySQL / PostgreSQL / GaussDB / SQLite / MongoDB / Oracle / 达梦 / SQL Server) use native table-level transfer, while Redis participates in a degraded mode through the fixed envelope table `__redis_keys`. Native Redis keyspace fidelity (stream consumer groups, cross-version `DUMP`, logical databases `dbN`) is out of scope.

Dialect differences are handled inside the adapters, which expose a uniform `?` placeholder and standard result sets to upper layers.

---

## Core capabilities

### Model tool `DatabaseManager`

A single tool with multiple actions, which reduces ambiguity for the model when choosing tools:

| action | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `list_connections` | List available connections (credentials not included) |
| `query` | Run a read-only query and return columns and rows |
| `execute` | Run a write statement; dangerous operations require confirmation |
| `schema` | View database / table / column structure |
| `preview` | Preview table data (paginated, up to 50 rows per page) |
| `run_script` | Run a script in a sandbox, which can call `db.query` / `db.execute` multiple times |

pkdxtools/pkdx.body:
# pkdx

A team-building support tool for Pokémon battles.
You can build teams, design movesets, calculate damage, and run battle simulations while chatting with Claude Code / Codex.

## Features

- **Team building**: Once you choose a core Pokémon, it interactively guides you through type coverage, speed tuning, and metagame counters. It proposes 6-Pokémon teams and 3-Pokémon selection patterns. You can also register teams from battle team screenshots in Champions.
- **Damage calculation**: Calculates random-roll damage including abilities, held items, weather, and Tera. It outputs practical KO numbers such as "guaranteed 2HKO" or "12/16 random 1HKO".
- **Training simulation**: Interactively sets nature, ability, held item, moves, and EVs, then calculates Lv50 actual stats. Completed builds can be saved to a file and used in team building.
- **Bulk/HP optimization**: Optimizes H/B/D EV distribution. Supports HP conditions (Berry / Sitrus Berry / Leftovers), physical/special weighting, and top-N candidate selection, and presents the distribution that maximizes the HBD value.
- **Pokémon search**: Searches Pokémon by conditions such as name, type, speed, and learnable moves. You can also quickly look up move lists and type matchups.
- **Battle simulation**: Uses two registered teams to simulate everything from team selection to battle results. Derives win rates when both sides keep making optimal moves.
- **Build articles and blog management**: Publishes build blogs based on registered battle team data. You can also create blogs that are not tied to a build.

## Supported Versions

- Shared data (e.g. `scarlet_violet`): https://github.com/towakey/pokedex/
- Champions regulation: https://github.com/projectpokemon/champout/ is used as the input source

## Setup

### A. If you want to save data to the cloud (with a GitHub account)

With a GitHub account, you can back up the teams and training data you create to the cloud, share them across multiple PCs, and restore past data.

1. Click the "Fork" button at the top right of the [pkdxtools/pkdx](https://github.com/pkdxtools/pkdx) GitHub page.
2. Pass the URL of your cloned repository to Claude Code / Codex and say "I want to use this."
3. After that, you can follow the latest version with the `/self-update` skill.

# DSH-Reforge

**DSH-Reforge (npm package name `dsh-reforge`) is a community plugin for DeepSeek Harness that accumulates traceable experience from test-verified Python bug fixes, and selects applicable experience as a reference for later similar tasks.**

DSH-Reforge is a DeepSeek Harness plugin for traceable experience from test-verified Python bug fixes, with scoped retrieval for later tasks.

**This release: `dsh-reforge@0.1.0-alpha.2`, experimental alpha.** It includes the new workbench, complete examples, configuration checks, and backup and restore. Whether the public npm/Release has been verified is subject to the [release status](https://github.com/wang1299/dsh-reforge/blob/HEAD/docs/release-status.md) and [Issue #113](https://github.com/wang1299/dsh-reforge/issues/113). This project is independently developed by the community and does not represent official DeepSeek review, recommendation, or security certification.

Precisely compatible with DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.5`, using an independent adaptation layer and Windows/Linux four-combination checks; scope is in the [version matrix](https://github.com/wang1299/dsh-reforge/blob/HEAD/docs/dsh-version-matrix.md). The old public alpha.1 only supported the previous host; other DSH versions require separate verification.

## What it can do

The development branch T074 adds [memory maintenance checks](https://github.com/wang1299/dsh-reforge/blob/HEAD/docs/memory-maintenance.md): explicit read-only checks of sources, fact references, and current code/dependency conditions. It distinguishes matches, items needing revision and re-verification, ineligible items, and unknown items, and provides paginated suggestions. `npm run memory:demo` runs three controls using real synthetic sources. It does not automatically revise or run tests, does not call models, and is not yet merged or released.

The development branch T073 provides an [acceptance-driven repair agent example](https://github.com/wang1299/dsh-reforge/blob/HEAD/examples/repair-agent/README.md): structured dependency planning, four native task tools, bounded replanning, and independent tests, connected to existing experience retrieval and budgeted context. Responses are scripted simulations; the tools and acceptance checks actually run. It is not yet merged or released and does not represent real model planning or its benefits.

xJogger/MangaAlpha.description: Komga-compatible comic server with lazy remote CBZ/CBR page streaming.
xJogger/MangaAlpha.body:
# MangaAlpha

**MangaAlpha** (formerly `fake-komga-115`) is a **100% pure Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), single-file, self-contained** lightweight Komga-compatible comic library and reading server. It also ships as a standalone Android app.

It unifies the **115 cloud drive**, **server-local / SMB mounted directories**, and **WebDAV (CloudDrive2 / OpenList / NAS)** into one library, with support for multi-source layered union libraries. It includes a **responsive web bookshelf and reading history timeline**, a **Simplified Chinese dual-page web reader with automatic white-margin cropping**, a **dual-engine Bangumi (`bgm.tv`) metadata scraping center that uses a Chinese synopsis-enhancing mirror by default**, **cross-platform update detection**, and an **AI Agent library governance API**. It is fully compatible with **Mihon (Komga extension)**, **Koharia**, and **KOReader (OPDS v1.2 + OPDS-PSE)** clients.

```text
Built-in web bookshelf (/) · Reading history (/history) · Simplified Chinese reader (/reader/*) · Mihon / Koharia · KOReader OPDS · AI Agent (/api/agent/v1)
                       ↓ (Session Cookie / HTTP Basic Auth / Bearer & X-API-Key)
                                     MangaAlpha
               ├── 115 Open API ──────────────→ downurl + HTTP Range chunked on-demand streaming decompression
               ├── WebDAV (CloudDrive2/OpenList) ─→ PROPFIND + token-bucket rate limiting + HTTP Range on-demand decompression
               └── Local / SMB mounted directories ────────→ native io.ReaderAt random direct reads (no chunked cache + empty mount point protection)
```

> **Core on-demand streaming promise**: During startup and directory scanning, only directory hierarchy and file size/modification time metadata are read. **Entire compressed archives are never downloaded in advance.** Only when a reader opens a volume and turns to a specific page are the byte ranges needed for that image read.
